mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate indicates easy monetary conditions, which may increase liquidity and boost equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly higher during periods of low FEDFUNDS (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rate indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days when UNRATE crosses above 9.5%.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in >40% of cases when UNRATE exceeds 9.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing real savings (RSAFS) reflects consumer strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth (INDPRO) above 95 indicates economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative in >50% of triggered cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) signals economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are not significantly higher (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: Low FEDFUNDS coupled with high UNRATE indicates policy support, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1) with high inflation (CPIAUCSL) may lead to rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in >40% of cases with high GDPC1 and CPIAUCSL.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening cycle, rising FEDFUNDS increases borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days when FEDFUNDS crosses 0.5%.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive in >30% of triggered cases.
